text:
Aisha (Finance): Quick billing update — planned metering + invoice format changes. Effective 2026-06-15 (UTC). TL;DR: invoices will consolidate low-volume line items into a single 'metering-smooth' bucket and metering will use a 60s smoothing window for rate-limit and overage calculations. No unit price changes.

Tom (Billing): What does "consolidate" mean for startups on free tiers? Will their credits still show per-model?

Aisha (Finance): Good Q. For accounts with < $10/mo usage we will show a single consolidated line instead of dozens of tiny per-model lines. Credits will still be applied before consolidation; invoice will show a 'credits applied' line and a single post-credit total. We'll include a downloadable CSV with full detail for reconciliation.

Lina (Support): How do we tell customers? Any automated notice?

Aisha (Finance): We'll send a staged email to all active bill payers on 2026-05-25, post an expanded docs page, and a banner in Console. Support template will be posted to #support by 2026-05-18. I'll ping you when it's live.

MJ (Engineering): Technical note: metering switch means rate-limit math moves from per-second buckets to a 60s smoothing window. This affects short burst behaviour only (not sustained throughput). We'll add new headers to API responses: X-RI-RateLimit-Window=60 and X-RI-Consumed-Smooth. No auth changes.

Tom (Billing): Any effect on grace/overage policy? Customers hit hard by bursts previously complained about surprise charges.

Aisha (Finance): We're introducing a 'soft-overage buffer' for the first 48 hours after the change for accounts with recurring invoices — we won't auto-bill > $100 in unapproved overage in that window; instead we'll flag and reach out. This is temporary for the migration period.

billing-bot: [automated] Migration job scheduled: 2026-06-15 00:00 UTC. Dry-run logs will be available at /billing/migration-dryruns/1876543210.

Lina (Support): Can we get a short FAQ snippet to paste into responses? Something like: "Why did my invoice line items change?" + a one-sentence answer.

Aisha (Finance): Yes — I'll draft an FAQ. Short answer: "We consolidated tiny line items to make invoices easier to read; your charges and credits are unchanged and you can download full usage CSVs for reconciliation." Use that for now.

MJ (Engineering): Will the rate-limit headers be backfilled for older logs? We should ensure our observability shows pre/post identical expected behaviour.

Aisha (Finance): We'll backfill per-request metering data for 30 days into the console's usage view. Engineering will coordinate the backfill job with infra.

Tom (Billing): Noted. Any exemptions for large enterprise customers who want per-model line items forever?

Aisha (Finance): Yes — enterprise accounts can request 'detailed billing' as an account setting; we'll keep current detailed exports for them. Contact me or @tom if you want to add to the allowlist.

Lina (Support): I'll queue a canned response and add to shared macros.

Aisha (Finance): Action items: 1) Support to post template by 2026-05-18 (Lina) 2) Docs + Console banner by 2026-05-25 (Docs/Platform) 3) Migration dry-run review next week (MJ/Tom) 4) Enterprise allowlist requests to billing@redwood.ai. Ping me for exceptions. Thanks :white_check_mark:

Tom (Billing): Thanks — will coordinate and share dry-run findings.

MJ (Engineering): I'll post the API header PR and dry-run logs link in #eng-runtime.

billing-bot: [automated] Reminder scheduled: notify-support: 2026-05-17 09:00 UTC.

Aisha (Finance): If anyone wants to preview the new invoice sample, see snippet below (example):

```
Invoice 2026-06-15
- Usage (metering-smooth): $72.43
- Credits applied: -$20.00
- Tax: $5.10
- Total due: $57.53
Details CSV available for download.
``` 

Aisha (Finance): Questions? Concerns? I'll collect them here and loop in legal if needed.
